Measure how stable a proportion is at each delay day of a reporting triangle

Source: R/proportion_stability.R
proportion_stability_v1.Rd

For each delay day, compares the proportion of numerator to denominator seen at that day with its settled value. Use it next to reporting_completion_v1() to see how many recent weeks of a proportion are reliable.

Usage

proportion_stability_v1(
  triangle,
  max_delay_days,
  denominator_col,
  delay_window = NULL
)

Arguments

triangle

The csfmt_reporting_triangle_v3 to measure. The value column of the triangle is the numerator.

max_delay_days

The delay horizon in days, delay day 0 to max_delay_days - 1.

denominator_col

The name of the column of triangle that holds the denominator.

delay_window

Use only the settled weeks of about this many recent weeks. It counts weeks, not days. NULL uses every settled week.

Value

A data.table with one row per series and delay day: the identity columns, n_settled, n_eval, delay, pct_count, prop_relerr_p50, prop_relerr_p90, prop_abserr_p50 and prop_abserr_p90.

  • n_settled: the settled weeks that the function uses.

  • n_eval: the weeks of n_settled with a cumulative denominator above 0 at delay day delay.

  • delay: the delay day, an integer from 0 to max_delay_days - 1.

  • pct_count: the pooled cumulative numerator at delay, in percent of the pooled settled numerator, over the n_settled weeks. It has 1 decimal.

  • prop_relerr_p50, prop_relerr_p90: the median and the 90th percentile of 100 * abs(p_d / p - 1), in percent of the settled proportion.

  • prop_abserr_p50, prop_abserr_p90: the median and the 90th percentile of 100 * abs(p_d - p), in percentage points.

The four error columns use stats::quantile(type = 7) over the n_eval weeks, and have 2 decimals. They are NA where n_eval is 0. The result is an empty data.table when no series has 3 weeks to use.

Details

Both counts come from reporting_triangle_matrix(). The settled value of a week is its cumulative count at delay day max_delay_days - 1. A report at delay max_delay_days or later is not in it. This is the convention of delay_distribution_v1(). It is different from reporting_completion_v1(), which adds the reports past the horizon to the last delay day.

A week is settled when its Monday is at least max_delay_days - 1 days before the as-of date, attr(triangle, "as_of"). A settled week is used only if its settled numerator and its settled denominator are both above 0. A series with fewer than 3 such weeks gets no rows, and no warning.

At delay day d, a week has the proportion p_d, its cumulative numerator divided by its cumulative denominator. Its settled proportion is p. A week with a cumulative denominator of 0 at day d is not used at that day.

See also

Other reporting completion functions: reporting_completion_trend_v1(), reporting_completion_v1()

Examples

monday <- as.Date("2023-01-02") + 7 * rep(0:19, each = 2)
d <- data.table::data.table(
  isoyearweek_reference = format(monday, "%G-%V"),
  reporting_date = monday + rep(c(1, 8), 20),
  numerator = rep(c(3, 1), 20),
  denominator = rep(c(10, 10), 20),
  indicator = "x", location = "nation", age = "total", sex = "total"
)
tri <- csfmt_reporting_triangle_v3(
  d,
  id_cols = c("indicator", "location", "age", "sex")
)

# The proportion is 0.3 on day 1 and 0.2 when it settles on day 8, so the
# relative error is 50 percent from day 1 to day 7.
ps <- proportion_stability_v1(tri, max_delay_days = 9, "denominator")
ps[, .(delay, n_eval, pct_count, prop_relerr_p50, prop_abserr_p50)]
#>    delay n_eval pct_count prop_relerr_p50 prop_abserr_p50
#>    <int>  <int>     <num>           <num>           <num>
#> 1:     0      0         0              NA              NA
#> 2:     1     20        75              50              10
#> 3:     2     20        75              50              10
#> 4:     3     20        75              50              10
#> 5:     4     20        75              50              10
#> 6:     5     20        75              50              10
#> 7:     6     20        75              50              10
#> 8:     7     20        75              50              10
#> 9:     8     20       100               0               0
